methodological_questions: Does adherence to the recommended mix predict winning once team quality is controlled?
Is the recommended mix derived independently of outcomes and of the games being predicted?
Can 54 series detect the plausible effect size?
Is adherence measured reliably given how many triggers lack a defined recommendation?

historical_evidence.finding: Series-level AVOID share vs winning: rho=-0.26, p=0.07 (n=50 series), underpowered, with about 80 series needed for p<0.05. Game-level rho=-0.19, p=0.008 used inflated n and was confounded by team quality. Recorded verdict: inconclusive.

BEST-minus-AVOID run-rate difference vs series wins, n=55 series. After controlling for talent, the adaptation coefficient has p=0.2755 (cluster p=0.2449) while talent has p=0.0213 (cluster p=0.0095). The record states n~55 cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality.
BEST/AVOID run rates vs series wins, n=110 series-directions. Spearman BEST rho=+0.131 (p=0.17) and AVOID rho=-0.098 (p=0.31). INSUFF_EVIDENCE is 91.5% of triggers. Recorded verdict: null.

In holdout games, closer alignment to the model's recommended mix was associated with higher efficiency: raw gap +5.18 ORtg, strength-controlled +3.27 ORtg (n=908 team-game rows). The outcome is efficiency, not winning. Model regret is non-negative by construction, and validation was same-pipeline with no CI stated.
After suppression, teams do not shift toward the BEST counter: BEST share 10.0%->10.2%, average pickup +0.0024 pp (n=591 triggers). Recorded as an adequately powered null.
Descriptive team BEST-share profiles. Win% is not identified with BEST share (e.g. IND 4.5% BEST with 71% win; ORL 59.3% AVOID with 0% win). No inferential test of stability vs noise.
Suppression profiles for stars. Rank-1 suppressor deltas are mostly within 1-2 SE with no multiple-comparison control.
Top-suppressor identity is stable across seasons for only 2/30 stars (min n=20 per cell), so suppressor-specific recommendations are unstable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-level AVOID share vs winning without adequate talent control
failed_approaches.why: n=50 gave p=0.07 and needed about 80 series; the game-level result was inflated by team-quality confounding (OKC disciplined and good).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Adaptation (BEST minus AVOID) as a series-win predictor after talent control
failed_approaches.why: Adaptation p=0.275 after talent control; n~55 series cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality.

failed_approaches.what_failed: BEST/AVOID run-rate alignment vs series wins
failed_approaches.why: Spearman correlations were not significant at n=110 directions, and INSUFF_EVIDENCE made up 91.5% of triggers, so adherence is thinly measured.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Expecting teams to move toward the BEST counter after suppression
failed_approaches.why: BEST pickup was essentially zero (+0.24 pp), so there is little adherence variation to exploit.

evidence_establishes: Three earlier series-level attempts (FAM:SF-CHT-039, FAM:SF-APPS-027, FAM:SF-APPS-030) at n of about 50-55 series, or 110 series-directions, did not produce a significant adherence-win association once team quality or power was considered.
Talent was a significant series-win predictor (p=0.0213) where adaptation was not (p=0.2755) in FAM:SF-APPS-027.
The only supported record (FAM:SF-APPM-001) concerns game-level efficiency, not winning, and was validated within the same pipeline.
Teams show little systematic shift toward BEST after suppression (FAM:SF05, powered null).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether adherence has a true small independent effect on series or game winning. The records show underpowered, confounded estimates rather than a powered null at the series level.
Whether the recommended mix is derived without leakage from the games where adherence is scored.
Whether a design with series fixed effects, a larger sample or a continuous adherence measure would detect an effect.
Whether the efficiency-alignment result from FAM:SF-APPM-001 translates into wins.
own_inferences: With 54 series, a rho near 0.1-0.26 and a talent control that absorbs most of the variance, power is likely below 30-40%, so the question as posed is largely untestable at the series level.

Adherence may be partly an outcome of game state or team quality: leading teams and better teams may be able to run their preferred plays. A positive raw association could therefore be reverse causation or talent confounding.
The sparse recommendation coverage (INSUFF_EVIDENCE 91.5%) means any adherence score is based on about 8% of triggers and is noisy, which biases estimates toward zero.
The one positive record (FAM:SF-APPM-001) is partly mechanical, since regret is non-negative by construction, and it is not evidence about winning.

The 54-series count likely includes partial 2025-26 playoffs, since the playoffs complete on 2026-06-21. A pre-registered test should be frozen before the full sample is known and then rerun on the complete one.
uncertainties: How adherence is operationalised in the question (run rate, L1 distance to the recommended mix, BEST-minus-AVOID) is not specified.
How the recommendation is built (training window, whether the opponent's own series games are included) is not stated in the task.
Whether the 54 series include the incomplete 2025-26 playoff series, and which series are included, is unknown.
The full text of records cut in the retrieval output was not read.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history this could look like a straightforward testable hypothesis. Three prior attempts at nearly identical series-level data were underpowered or null after talent control and were recorded as untestable. This moves the decision away from running the same 54-series test again and toward a redesigned, pre-registered test. The positive efficiency record (FAM:SF-APPM-001) does not change this, since it is a different outcome.

blocking_constraints.text: 54 series; FAM:SF-CHT-039 recorded about 80 series needed for p<0.05 at rho about -0.26 before adjusting for talent, and more would be needed after adjustment.
Team quality drives both adherence and winning; FAM:SF-APPS-027 adaptation p=0.275 after talent control.
INSUFF_EVIDENCE is 91.5% of triggers (FAM:SF-APPS-030), so few triggers have a defined recommendation.

prior_work.summary: Substantially the same series-level question was examined three times with n of about 50-55 series. Results were inconclusive or null and untestable after talent control. Game-level efficiency alignment was supported (FAM:SF-APPM-001), but that outcome is not winning. The question is not decisively answered.

risks.text: Series count is too small to detect modest effects after covariate adjustment.
Talent, opponent strength and game state confound adherence and winning; game-level analysis inflates n and mixes between-team quality with adherence.
If the recommended mix is fit on data including the evaluated series or games, adherence is partly defined by outcomes.
BEST/AVOID labels are derived from PPP outcomes, so adherence to them is mechanically related to scoring, which correlates with winning.
Most triggers have no recommendation defined, so the adherence measure is based on few events.
Adherence is a noisy, low-coverage measure, and suppressor identity is unstable across seasons (FAM:SF-APPA-058).
Several adherence definitions and the BEST-vs-AVOID split offer analytic flexibility, and the earlier families had no multiplicity control.
Recommendations and league tactics may shift across seasons, so a pooled recommendation may not transfer.

design.estimand: Within-series, game-level association between a team's adherence to a recommended mix (derived out of sample) and winning that game, conditional on series fixed effects and pre-game strength, expressed as an odds ratio per 1 SD of adherence.
design.unit: Team-game within series (primary); series-level win as a secondary, descriptive analysis only.
design.sample: Playoff series from 2022-23 to 2024-25 plus 2025-26 playoffs, frozen at the time of pre-registration and then re-run on the complete 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21). Recommendations come only from data before each series, using prior seasons and the regular season. Only triggers with a defined BEST/AVOID recommendation are scored, and the rest are reported as a coverage fraction.
design.power: Series level: about 80 series are needed for p<0.05 at rho 0.26 without talent control (FAM:SF-CHT-039), and more with control; 54 series is therefore underpowered. Run a simulation-based power analysis before the test, with a minimum detectable odds ratio stated. If power for the plausible effect is under 0.5, declare the test untestable rather than run it.
design.controls: Series fixed effects (absorb talent), pre-game net rating and rest, home court, and score-state or time-in-game to address reverse causation; cluster standard errors by series and team.
design.falsification: Placebo: adherence computed against a recommendation from a shuffled opponent or a different season should show no association. Also check that the adherence-win relation does not appear using the pre-trigger mix, which would indicate game-state reverse causation.
design.multiplicity: One primary adherence definition fixed in advance (BEST share minus AVOID share among defined triggers). Alternatives are secondary, with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Call the question supported only if the primary odds ratio's 95% CI excludes 1 in the predicted direction, the placebo is null and the effect is robust to leave-one-season-out. Call it a null only if the CI excludes the minimum effect of interest. Otherwise report it as inconclusive or untestable.
design.data_version: NBA per-game files and derived play-type records for 2022-23 through 2025-26; freeze the data snapshot and the 2025-26 playoff state on the pre-registration date, and record the re-run after 2026-06-21.

methodological_questions: Does adherence to a recommended play-type mix predict winning a series or game?
How is the recommended mix derived and is it leaked from outcomes or look-ahead data?
Is 54 series sufficient power, and what confounders (team quality, opponent strength) affect adherence-win associations?
args.query: suppression-conditional recommended mix adherence predicts winning; best/avoid play-type recommendations against defensive suppression; series-level test with 54 series

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether to pull up one more family, but the budget allows it and I don't think it's necessary, so I'll wrap up now. The main question is whether sticking to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning, across 54 series, and the earlier family SF-CHT-039 showed a weak, non-significant negative correlation, so the evidence is inconclusive.

Now I'm weighing the remaining series against the power I'd need: around 80 series to reach significance at that correlation, and more once talent is controlled for. The 2025-26 playoffs are still partway through, so the count of 54 likely leaves out incomplete series. My rough odds put the question mostly in "untestable," so I'm leaning toward not proceeding as posed and considering a game-level analysis with team-clustered effects instead.

I'm settling on do_not_proceed for the series-level test as posed, since three earlier attempts on this same data came back inconclusive and a fourth with 54 series wouldn't add much. I'll note the recorded statuses: SF-CHT-039 as untestable with an inconclusive verdict, and SF-APPM-001 as supported.

I'm marking the remaining families as recorded: SF-APPS-027 and SF-APPS-030 untestable, SF05 rejected, SF-APPM-022 inconclusive, and APPA-058 rejected.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether to pull up one more family, but the budget allows it and I don't think it's necessary, so I'll wrap up now. The main question is whether sticking to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning, across 54 series, and the earlier family SF-CHT-039 showed a weak, non-significant negative correlation, so the evidence is inconclusive.

Now I'm weighing the remaining series against the power I'd need: around 80 series to reach significance at that correlation, and more once talent is controlled for. The 2025-26 playoffs are still partway through, so the count of 54 likely leaves out incomplete series. My rough odds put the question mostly in "untestable," so I'm leaning toward not proceeding as posed and considering a game-level analysis with team-clustered effects instead.

I'm settling on do_not_proceed for the series-level test as posed, since three earlier attempts on this same data came back inconclusive and a fourth with 54 series wouldn't add much. I'll note the recorded statuses: SF-CHT-039 as untestable with an inconclusive verdict, and SF-APPM-001 as supported.

I'm marking the remaining families as recorded: SF-APPS-027 and SF-APPS-030 untestable, SF05 rejected, SF-APPM-022 inconclusive, and APPA-058 rejected.
